searchable_text: samples Number of Samples integer Density of samples over surface. Higher sample numbers generate more accurate results, at a cost of computation time. 50 is a resonable starting number. iterations Blurring Iterations integer How much to blur the sample colours. At low values the sample regions will be visible as patches. At high values the samples will be overblurred, missing lighting detail. Ideally aim for enough blur to blend the sample patches together. Enabling 'visualize lighting' can help to see how much the patches are being blurred together. grouptype Group Type ordinal  ao_brightening AO Brightening toggle Toggle to enable the brightening of crevices and overhangs via interted ambient occlusion. ao_strength AO Strength float How much to brighten occluded areas. Aim to make crevices blend in with unoccluded neighbouring areas. Values which are too low will appear shadowed, values which are too high will make crevices glow. ao_blend_strength AO Blend Strength float An additional mixing control to blend the edges of the AO regions. ao_iterations AO Blurring Iterations integer  ao_tint AO Tint float Amount to increase the brightness of the AO regions, adjust this until the dark crevices blend into their neighbours. lighting_exposure Lighting Exposure float Multiplier for the lighting visualizer if it is too overexposed or underexposed in the viewport. lighting_saturation Lighting Saturation float  vis_lighting Visualize Lighting toggle Display the blurred and extracted lighting result only. The default [\ cryptomatte# Cryptomatte toggle Enable this to turn this image plane into Cryptomatte layer. See Cryptomatte for more info. cryptomatterank# Overlap Limit integer Maximum number of IDs that can be stored in a single pixel. A value of 6 is recommended.  cryptomattesidecar# Manifest File string Optional external manifest file. It will be saved into same directory as the render product. If this path is unspecified, the manifest will be embedded into render product as metadata.  dooutputcs# Output Colorspace toggle Specify the OCIO color output space for the component.  outputcs# Output Colorspace string Specify the OCIO color output space for the component.  denoiser Denoiser string Choose a denoiser to run on the finished image output, or No Denoiser. This utility currently supports Intel Open Image Denoise (included with Houdini) and the NVIDIA OptiX Denoiser (must be installed separately). You must be on a supported platform and have the chosen denoising library installed for this to work. denoise_usealbedo Use Albedo toggle Some denoising libraries can use albedo to get a better sense of the image, guiding how and where it reduces noise. denoise_useN Use N Input toggle Some denoising libraries can use normals to get a better sense of the image, guiding how and where it reduces noise. denoise_aovs AOVs string Space-separated list of AOVs to run the denoiser on. sepparm30 Spacer separator  tonemap Tone Map string The basic idea behind tone mapping is the conversion from HDR real world luminances to LDR display values, i.e. for making images displayable on monitors. Another aspect is to simulate a particular film look. Film material is designed to have a certain â€œresponseâ€� to light to enhance contrast and colors, represented as a characteristic curve. A filmic tone mapping curve is subdivided into toe, shoulder and linear sections for an imageâ€™s dark, bright, and mid tones. Houdini provides several common operators for filmic tone mapping and each operator applies a specific S-shaped tone mapping curve. tonemapcurve Tonemap Curve ramp_flt Tone map curves apply to the Reinhard, Unreal, Aces and Hable operators. The curve is a visual representation of the mathematical model of each operator. You can fine-tune tone mapping through the curveâ€™s control points. tonemap_aovs AOVs string Space-separated list of AOVs that will be affected by the chosen Tone Map operator. tonemap_toe Toe float This parameter applies to the Hable, Hable2 and Unreal operators and ranges between 0 and 1. The default values for Hable and Hable2 is 0.5. For Unreal, the default value is 0.55. The value controls the strength (curvature) of the toe segment in dark areas. Higher values create a darker image, smaller values brighten the dark tones. tonemap_shoulder Shoulder float This parameter applies to the Hable, Hable2 and Unreal operators and ranges between 0and 1. The default values for Hable and Hable2 is 0.5. For Unreal, the default value is 0.26. Shoulder controls to curveâ€™s amount of curvature for bright tone values. The value affects where the shoulder curve starts in the graph: a value of 1 means that the shoulder starts exactly where the toe ends. tonemap_utoe Toe float  tonemap_ushoulder Shoulder float  tonemap_slope Slope float This parameter applies to the Unreal operator and ranges between 0 and 1. The default value is 0.88. Controls the tone mapping curveâ€™s steepness, where higher settings (steeper curve) make the image darker and increase contrast; smaller values brighten the image and make it pale. tonemap_linear Linear float This parameter applies to the Hable operator and ranges between 0 and 2. The default value is 0.3. Tones in the linear section should not (or hardly) change during the tone mapping process and represent the imageâ€™s original tones. The Linear value describes the distance between toe and shoulder. Higher values mean that the tow and shoulder sections become smaller, while more tones remain unchanged: the overall curve becomes more linear. tonemap_linearangle Linear Angle float This parameter applies to the Hable operator and ranges between 0 and 1. The default value is 0.1. Here you control the slope of the linear part of the tone mapping curve. tonemap_toelength Toe Length float This parameter applies to the Hable2 operator and ranges between 0 and 1. The default value is 0.5. A small value creates a short toe section that quickly transitions into the linear section. A value of 0 eliminates the toe, and value of 1 means the toe takes up half the curve. Note that there are two ways to disable the toe: you can either set Toe Length or Toe to 0. tonemap_shoulderlength Shoulder Length float This parameter applies to the Hable2 operator and ranges between 0 and 1. The default value is 0.5. Shoulder Length describes how many F stops you want to add to the dynamic range of the curve. Here you control the transition point from the linear section to the shoulder section. tonemap_shoulderangle Shoulder Angle float This parameter applies to the Hable2 operator and ranges between 0 and 1. The default value is 1. Here you control how much overshoot you want to add the curveâ€™s shoulder. sepparm31 Spacer separator  ocio_enable# Enable toggle Enables the OCIO image filter defined below. ocio_planes# Planes string The render var names to which the OCIO image filter will be applied.  ocio_outputspace# Output Space string Specify the OCIO color output space the image filter will apply.  ocio_inputspace# Input Space string In most cases this should be left at data. There may be some strange case where the source of the AOV is already in a defined color space, in which case you can specify the source space here.  ocio_looks# Looks string Space-separated list of looks to apply to the finished image. A â€œlookâ€� is a named OCIO color transform, usually intended to achieve an artistic effect. See the OCIO documentation for more information.  colorlimit_enable# Enable toggle Enables the color limit sample filter defined below.  colorlimit_planes# Planes string A space-separated list of AOV names to which this color limit will be applied.  colorlimit_limit# Limit float The maximum value a shading sample is allowed to contribute to these AOVs.  aspectRatioConformPolicy Aspect Ratio Conform Policy string What to do if the aspect ratio of the output image (Resolution width divided by height) doesnâ€™t match the aspect ratio of the camera aperture (controlled by attributes on the camera). This allows a standard renderer to do something reasonable when you switch between cameras. dataWindowNDC Data Window NDC float Directs the renderer to only render within this window of the entire output image. You specify the window as minX, minY, maxX, maxY, where each number is a normalized value from 0 to 1. 0, 0 is the bottom left, 1, 1 is the top right, 0.5, 0.5 is the center, and so on. The default is 0, 0, 1, 1 (no cropping). Note that you can use negative values. For example, -0.1, -0.1, 1.1, 1.1 will give you 10% overscan on each side. pixelAspectRatio Pixel Aspect Ratio float The aspect ratio (width/height) of image pixels (not the image itself). The default is 1.0, indicating square pixels. image_artist Artist string The name of the person, department, or studio that created the image file. The node will set this field on the output image if the image format supports metadata (for example, .exr).  image_comment Comment string An arbitrary comment, for example a description of the purpose of the output image. The node will set this field on the output image if the image format supports metadata (for example, .exr). image_hostname Hostname string The name of the computer that generated this the output file. The node will set this field on the output image if the image format supports metadata (for example, .exr). image_exr_compression EXR Compression string Sets the compression for saved OpenEXR files. When saving multi-part OpenEXR files, you can specify compression per AOV through a Render Var LOP. image_dwa_compression DWA Compression Level float  dcm DCM toggle Generate a deep camera map image recording depth. dcmfilename DCM Filename file The filename to save the deep camera map image to (this should be an .exr file).  dcmvars DCM Render Vars string Space separated list of RenderVar prim paths (not a list of AOV names). These must be the fully qualified path to the RenderVar prim and the render var name. You can use patterns to match multiple prims. The default is /Render/Products/Vars/*, which matches all prims in the branch where Houdini usually creates RenderVar prims. You can also leave this field empty to omit all RenderVars and only include alpha and depth planes (like a Deep Shadow Map). dcmcompression DCM Compression integer Compression value between 0 and 10. Used to limit the number of samples which are stored in a lossy compression mode for volume samples. The compression parameter determines the maximum possible error in scalar channels for each sample. For compression greater than 0, the following relationship holds: Error = 1/(2^(10-compression)) dcmofsize DCM Of Size ordinal Opacity is usually computed as a full-color value and stored as such. To cut down on file size, if full color is not needed, this settings can be used to store a monochromatic version of the full color value. Set this value to 1 for monochrome, 3 for full color. dcmzbias DCM Z-Bias float Used in compression to merge together samples which are closer than the given threshold. Samples that are closer together than this bias value are merged into a single sample whose z-front and z-back span encompasses all the merged samples. setlayerrendersettings Set as Default Render Settings Prim toggle A layer in USD can define a default render settings primitive for husk or other tools to use when rendering. convergence_mode Convergence Mode string When set to Path Traced, maximum of 1 indirect ray is generated per bounce. When set to Automatic, the number of indirect rays is calculated based on initial noise estimate, target noise threshold, and the maximum number of camera rays. Also note that under Automatic mode, number ofsamples for direct lighting is adjusted based on noise estimate as well. oracle Pixel Oracle string When rendering, a Pixel Oracle tells karma which pixels need additional sampling and which pixels are converged. This parameter tells karma which oracle to use. oracle_minsamples Minimum Samples integer The minimum number of camera rays (primary samples) for each pixel.  oracle_plane Plane string The AOV to use to measure variance.  oracle_variance Variance Threshold float The amount of variance that triggers more rays.  randomseed Random Seed integer Variance sampling involves some randomness. You can change this number to get slightly different results.  oracle_ociomode OCIO Transform ordinal Whether to apply an OCIO transform to the pixels before measuring variance.  oracle_ociodisplay Display string  oracle_ocioview View string  oracle_ociocolorspace Color Space string  varianceaa_thresh Noise Level float Noise threshold to determine the number of indirect rays cast for indirect bounce when the Convergence Mode is set to Automatic. Decreasing this threshold (for example, to 0.001) will theoretically send more indirect rays and decrease noise, however the â€œextraâ€� rays will likely be cancelled out by the Max Ray Samples parameter. The correct way to decrease noise is to increase the number of samples per pixel, rather than change this threshold. guiding_enable Enable Indirect Guiding toggle When turned on, Karma does a pre-render to roughly estimate of the light in the scene, and uses that to guide indirect diffuse rays, rather than just relying on the BSDF sampling distribution. This can improve â€œdifficultâ€� lighting (for example, caustics, and mostly indirect lighting), but can make â€œeasyâ€� lighting noisier. Before using this, you can try rendering direct and indirect AOVs to see where the noise is. If the noise is mostly caused by the direct lighting, thereâ€™s no point in turning on path guiding. outputcheckpoint Output Checkpoint Files toggle When this is on, Karma will periodically write out image tile data to a checkpoint file. If the process is terminated before completing the render, you can resume it by turning on Resume from Checkpoint and restarting. productName Checkpoint File string When Output checkpoint files is on, the name of the checkpoint file to write to. The default ($HIP/render/$HIPNAME.$OS.$F4.checkpoint) puts the checkpoint file inside a render directory next to the current scene file, and includes the base name of the current scene file ($HIPNAME), this nodeâ€™s name ($OS), and the render frame ($F) in the filename to help avoid two processes trying to use the same checkpoint file at the same time. savefrequency Save Frequency float When Output checkpoint files is on, Karma waits this number of seconds between writing out a checkpoint file. The default is 60. resume Resume From Checkpoint toggle If this is on and you start a render and the renderer notices there is a valid checkpoint file, it will try to resume rendering from that checkpoint. If you want to restart the render from the beginning, you can turn this off or just delete the checkpoint file(s). imagemode Image Mode string Determines how the image will be rendered.  progressivepasses Progressive Passes integer When rendering in bucket mode (see imagemode), this is the number of progressive passes over the image to perform before switching to bucket mode. bucketsize Bucket Size integer Karma breaks down an image into multiple buckets for rendering. This is the side length (in pixels) of the square bucket. The default is 32, specifying a 32 pixel x 32 pixel bucket. Threads operate at the bucket level, so it might be useful to lower the bucket size if there are only a few buckets that are particularly expensive. That way the expensive areas can be divided across more threads. bucketorder Bucket Order string Specifies which buckets are rendered first. Values can be:  usecacheratio Cache Limit integer Whether to use a fixed size cache (karma:global:cachesize) or whether to use a proportion of physical memory (karma:global:cacheratio). cacheratio Cache Memory Ratio float The proportion of physical memory Karma will use for its unified cache. cachesize Cache Size (MB) integer  abortmissingtexture Cancel Render if Missing Texture is Discovered toggle Turning on this option will cause Karma to stop the render with an error if it encounters a missing texture map exportcomponents Export Components string A space-separated list of shading component names that will be computed for export. If you have defined new component labels in your materials, these can be added to the list so that they are exported for per-component export planes. If you are not using some components, remove them from the list to improve render efficiency. diffusecomponents Diffuse Components string A space-separated list of component types that will behave like diffuse bounces. This will affect which reflection scope is used based on the ray type and also which bounce limit to use. Uncategorized component types are assumed to be reflections. refractcomponents Refract Components string A space-separated list of component types that will behave like refract bounces. This will affect which reflection scope is used based on the ray type and also which bounce limit to use. Uncategorized component types are assumed to be reflections. volumecomponents Volume Components string A space-separated list of component types that will behave like volume bounces. This will affect which reflection scope is used based on the ray type and also which bounce limit to use. Uncategorized component types are assumed to be reflections. ssscomponents SSS Components string A space-separated list of component types that will behave like subsurface scatter bounces. This will affect which reflection scope is used based on the ray type and also which bounce limit to use. Uncategorized component types are assumed to be reflections. execute Render to Disk button Renders with the last render control settings. This blocks Houdini until the render completes. renderpreview Render to MPlay button Render directly into an MPlay preview window, instead of to an image file. (You can save the image to disk from inside MPlay.) executebackground Render to Disk in Background button Renders with the last render control settings in a background process. renderdialog Controls... button Click to open a dialog that lets you launch a â€œone-offâ€� render with different frame range and dependency settings. trange Valid Frame Range ordinal  f Start/End/Inc float When Valid frame range is â€œRender frame rangeâ€� or â€œRender frame range (strict)â€�, the start and end frames (inclusive) and interval. foffset Preroll/Postroll/Inc float When Valid frame range is â€œRender stageâ€™s frame rangeâ€�, the number of frames before and after the stageâ€™s official start and end frame to save, and the interval between time samples. allframesatonce Render All Frames With a Single Process toggle Render all frames in a background process. Default is off. This allows continued interaction with Houdini while the render process runs. override_camera Override Camera string Scene graph path to the Camera prim to render from. If this is blank, the node uses the camera specified on the render settings primitive. outputimage Override Output Image image If this is not blank, render to this file path instead of the output specified in the RenderSettings prim. When starting a new render process for each frame, this parameter can use standard Houdini variables such as $F4 to specify unique per-frame image files. When Render All Frames With a Single Process is enabled, this parameter must pass an un-expanded frame specifier (such as $F4 or <FF>) to husk. This may require the use of a backslash to prevent variable expansion when evaluating the parameter. primpattern Primitives string A space-separated list of prim paths for the objects you want to act as hold-outs.  spacer Spacer label  quicksetup3   ordinal  primpath Rendersettings Primitive Path string The prim path of a USD Render Settings prim to use to set up the background and matte settings. The default is /Render/rendersettings, which is the default for where the Karma render node looks for render settings. If this prim doesnâ€™t already exist in the incoming stage, this node will create it. plate Plate image The file path of the background image to use.  s Scale vector2  Horizontal and vertical scaling factors for the background image. These are normalized relative to the rendered image size, so for example a horizontal scale of 1 is the width of the rendered image. t Translate vector2 Horziontal and vertical offsets for the background image. These are normalized relative to the rendered images size, so for example a horizontal offset of 0.25 moves the background image to the right 1/4 of the width of the rendered image. useoffscreentex Use Offscreen Texture toggle If the background plate does not perfectly cover the camera view, the â€œrealâ€� background (empty space) will show through. Use this to replace empty space with a texture. If you leave this off, the node will fill empty space with the Offscreen color instead. offscreentex Offscreen Texture image When Use offscreen texture is on, the file path of the texture image to use to cover empty space. offscreentex_rotate Rotate vector When Use offscreen texture is on, this sets the rotation of the offscreen texture in 3D space. offscreen_col Offscreen Color color When Use offscreen texture is off, the color to use for any â€œempty spaceâ€� if the background plate does not fully cover the camera view. labelparm Shader Parameters label  metallic Metallic float Values closer to 1 give the shader a more metallic appearance. reflect Reflectivity float Controls the reflectivity of surfaces facing the viewer. This is also affected by the Index of Refraction. rough Roughness float Controls how dull a surface appears. A value of 0.0 results in a smooth surface with perfectly sharp reflections. A value of 1.0 produces a completely dull surface. ior IOR float Higher values reflect more light and bend refraction rays more. shadows Shadows ordinal Whether to record all holdout shadows in a single AOV, or generate a separate AOV for each light LPE tag. diffuse Diffuse toggle Generate an AOV for diffuse bounces on holdout objects.  emission Emission toggle Generate an AOV for light emissions on holdout objects.  reflection Glossy Reflection toggle Generate an AOV for glossy reflections on holdout objects. When disabled, the background shader will become diffuse only, reflectivity and metallic shader parameters will be set to 0. reflectionocclusion Reflection Occlusion ordinal When Glossy Reflection is enabled, whether to record all holdout reflection occlusion in a single AOV, or generate a separate AOV for each light LPE tag.

A value of 6 is recommended.  cryptomattesidecar# Manifest File string Optional external manifest file. It will be saved into same directory as the render product. If this path is unspecified, the manifest will be embedded into render product as metadata.  dooutputcs# Output Colorspace toggle Specify the OCIO color output space for the component.  outputcs# Output Colorspace string Specify the OCIO color output space for the component.  denoiser Denoiser string Choose a denoiser to run on the finished image output, or No Denoiser. This utility currently supports Intel Open Image Denoise (included with Houdini) and the NVIDIA OptiX Denoiser (must be installed separately). You must be on a supported platform and have the chosen denoising library installed for this to work. denoise_usealbedo Use Albedo toggle Some denoising libraries can use albedo to get a better sense of the image, guiding how and where it reduces noise. denoise_useN Use N Input toggle Some denoising libraries can use normals to get a better sense of the image, guiding how and where it reduces noise. denoise_aovs AOVs string Space-separated list of AOVs to run the denoiser on. sepparm30 Spacer separator  tonemap Tone Map string The basic idea behind tone mapping is the conversion from HDR real world luminances to LDR display values, i.e. for making images displayable on monitors. Another aspect is to simulate a particular film look. Film material is designed to have a certain â€œresponseâ€� to light to enhance contrast and colors, represented as a characteristic curve. A filmic tone mapping curve is subdivided into toe, shoulder and linear sections for an imageâ€™s dark, bright, and mid tones. Houdini provides several common operators for filmic tone mapping and each operator applies a specific S-shaped tone mapping curve. tonemapcurve Tonemap Curve ramp_flt Tone map curves apply to the Reinhard, Unreal, Aces and Hable operators. The curve is a visual representation of the mathematical model of each operator. You can fine-tune tone mapping through the curveâ€™s control points. tonemap_aovs AOVs string Space-separated list of AOVs that will be affected by the chosen Tone Map operator. tonemap_toe Toe float This parameter applies to the Hable, Hable2 and Unreal operators and ranges between 0 and 1. The default values for Hable and Hable2 is 0.5. For Unreal, the default value is 0.55. The value controls the strength (curvature) of the toe segment in dark areas. Higher values create a darker image, smaller values brighten the dark tones. tonemap_shoulder Shoulder float This parameter applies to the Hable, Hable2 and Unreal operators and ranges between 0and 1. The default values for Hable and Hable2 is 0.5. For Unreal, the default value is 0.26. Shoulder controls to curveâ€™s amount of curvature for bright tone values. The value affects where the shoulder curve starts in the graph: a value of 1 means that the shoulder starts exactly where the toe ends. tonemap_utoe Toe float  tonemap_ushoulder Shoulder float  tonemap_slope Slope float This parameter applies to the Unreal operator and ranges between 0 and 1. The default value is 0.88. Controls the tone mapping curveâ€™s steepness, where higher settings (steeper curve) make the image darker and increase contrast; smaller values brighten the image and make it pale. tonemap_linear Linear float This parameter applies to the Hable operator and ranges between 0 and 2. The default value is 0.3. Tones in the linear section should not (or hardly) change during the tone mapping process and represent the imageâ€™s original tones. The Linear value describes the distance between toe and shoulder. Higher values mean that the tow and shoulder sections become smaller, while more tones remain unchanged: the overall curve becomes more linear. tonemap_linearangle Linear Angle float This parameter applies to the Hable operator and ranges between 0 and 1. The default value is 0.1. Here you control the slope of the linear part of the tone mapping curve. tonemap_toelength Toe Length float This parameter applies to the Hable2 operator and ranges between 0 and 1. The default value is 0.5. A small value creates a short toe section that quickly transitions into the linear section. A value of 0 eliminates the toe, and value of 1 means the toe takes up half the curve. Note that there are two ways to disable the toe: you can either set Toe Length or Toe to 0. tonemap_shoulderlength Shoulder Length float This parameter applies to the Hable2 operator and ranges between 0 and 1. The default value is 0.5. Shoulder Length describes how many F stops you want to add to the dynamic range of the curve. Here you control the transition point from the linear section to the shoulder section. tonemap_shoulderangle Shoulder Angle float This parameter applies to the Hable2 operator and ranges between 0 and 1. The default value is 1. Here you control how much overshoot you want to add the curveâ€™s shoulder. sepparm31 Spacer separator  ocio_enable# Enable toggle Enables the OCIO image filter defined below. ocio_planes# Planes string The render var names to which the OCIO image filter will be applied.  ocio_outputspace# Output Space string Specify the OCIO color output space the image filter will apply.  ocio_inputspace# Input Space string In most cases this should be left at data. There may be some strange case where the source of the AOV is already in a defined color space, in which case you can specify the source space here.  ocio_looks# Looks string Space-separated list of looks to apply to the finished image. A â€œlookâ€� is a named OCIO color transform, usually intended to achieve an artistic effect. See the OCIO documentation for more information.  colorlimit_enable# Enable toggle Enables the color limit sample filter defined below.  colorlimit_planes# Planes string A space-separated list of AOV names to which this color limit will be applied.  colorlimit_limit# Limit float The maximum value a shading sample is allowed to contribute to these AOVs.  aspectRatioConformPolicy Aspect Ratio Conform Policy string What to do if the aspect ratio of the output image (Resolution width divided by height) doesnâ€™t match the aspect ratio of the camera aperture (controlled by attributes on the camera). This allows a standard renderer to do something reasonable when you switch between cameras. dataWindowNDC Data Window NDC float Directs the renderer to only render within this window of the entire output image. You specify the window as minX, minY, maxX, maxY, where each number is a normalized value from 0 to 1. 0, 0 is the bottom left, 1, 1 is the top right, 0.5, 0.5 is the center, and so on. The default is 0, 0, 1, 1 (no cropping). Note that you can use negative values. For example, -0.1, -0.1, 1.1, 1.1 will give you 10% overscan on each side. pixelAspectRatio Pixel Aspect Ratio float The aspect ratio (width/height) of image pixels (not the image itself). The default is 1.0, indicating square pixels. image_artist Artist string The name of the person, department, or studio that created the image file. The node will set this field on the output image if the image format supports metadata (for example, .exr).  image_comment Comment string An arbitrary comment, for example a description of the purpose of the output image. The node will set this field on the output image if the image format supports metadata (for example, .exr). image_hostname Hostname string The name of the computer that generated this the output file. The node will set this field on the output image if the image format supports metadata (for example, .exr). image_exr_compression EXR Compression string Sets the compression for saved OpenEXR files. When saving multi-part OpenEXR files, you can specify compression per AOV through a Render Var LOP. image_dwa_compression DWA Compression Level float  dcm DCM toggle Generate a deep camera map image recording depth. dcmfilename DCM Filename file The filename to save the deep camera map image to (this should be an .exr file).  dcmvars DCM Render Vars string Space separated list of RenderVar prim paths (not a list of AOV names). These must be the fully qualified path to the RenderVar prim and the render var name. You can use patterns to match multiple prims. The default is /Render/Products/Vars/*, which matches all prims in the branch where Houdini usually creates RenderVar prims. You can also leave this field empty to omit all RenderVars and only include alpha and depth planes (like a Deep Shadow Map). dcmcompression DCM Compression integer Compression value between 0 and 10. Used to limit the number of samples which are stored in a lossy compression mode for volume samples. The compression parameter determines the maximum possible error in scalar channels for each sample. For compression greater than 0, the following relationship holds: Error = 1/(2^(10-compression)) dcmofsize DCM Of Size ordinal Opacity is usually computed as a full-color value and stored as such. To cut down on file size, if full color is not needed, this settings can be used to store a monochromatic version of the full color value. Set this value to 1 for monochrome, 3 for full color. dcmzbias DCM Z-Bias float Used in compression to merge together samples which are closer than the given threshold. Samples that are closer together than this bias value are merged into a single sample whose z-front and z-back span encompasses all the merged samples. setlayerrendersettings Set as Default Render Settings Prim toggle A layer in USD can define a default render settings primitive for husk or other tools to use when rendering. convergence_mode Convergence Mode string When set to Path Traced, maximum of 1 indirect ray is generated per bounce. When set to Automatic, the number of indirect rays is calculated based on initial noise estimate, target noise threshold, and the maximum number of camera rays. Also note that under Automatic mode, number ofsamples for direct lighting is adjusted based on noise estimate as well. oracle Pixel Oracle string When rendering, a Pixel Oracle tells karma which pixels need additional sampling and which pixels are converged. This parameter tells karma which oracle to use. oracle_minsamples Minimum Samples integer The minimum number of camera rays (primary samples) for each pixel.  oracle_plane Plane string The AOV to use to measure variance.  oracle_variance Variance Threshold float The amount of variance that triggers more rays.  randomseed Random Seed integer Variance sampling involves some randomness. You can change this number to get slightly different results.  oracle_ociomode OCIO Transform ordinal Whether to apply an OCIO transform to the pixels before measuring variance.  oracle_ociodisplay Display string  oracle_ocioview View string  oracle_ociocolorspace Color Space string  varianceaa_thresh Noise Level float Noise threshold to determine the number of indirect rays cast for indirect bounce when the Convergence Mode is set to Automatic. Decreasing this threshold (for example, to 0.001) will theoretically send more indirect rays and decrease noise, however the â€œextraâ€� rays will likely be cancelled out by the Max Ray Samples parameter. The correct way to decrease noise is to increase the number of samples per pixel, rather than change this threshold. guiding_enable Enable Indirect Guiding toggle When turned on, Karma does a pre-render to roughly estimate of the light in the scene, and uses that to guide indirect diffuse rays, rather than just relying on the BSDF sampling distribution. This can improve â€œdifficultâ€� lighting (for example, caustics, and mostly indirect lighting), but can make â€œeasyâ€� lighting noisier. Before using this, you can try rendering direct and indirect AOVs to see where the noise is. If the noise is mostly caused by the direct lighting, thereâ€™s no point in turning on path guiding. outputcheckpoint Output Checkpoint Files toggle When this is on, Karma will periodically write out image tile data to a checkpoint file. If the process is terminated before completing the render, you can resume it by turning on Resume from Checkpoint and restarting. productName Checkpoint File string When Output checkpoint files is on, the name of the checkpoint file to write to. The default ($HIP/render/$HIPNAME.$OS.$F4.checkpoint) puts the checkpoint file inside a render directory next to the current scene file, and includes the base name of the current scene file ($HIPNAME), this nodeâ€™s name ($OS), and the render frame ($F) in the filename to help avoid two processes trying to use the same checkpoint file at the same time. savefrequency Save Frequency float When Output checkpoint files is on, Karma waits this number of seconds between writing out a checkpoint file. The default is 60. resume Resume From Checkpoint toggle If this is on and you start a render and the renderer notices there is a valid checkpoint file, it will try to resume rendering from that checkpoint. If you want to restart the render from the beginning, you can turn this off or just delete the checkpoint file(s). imagemode Image Mode string Determines how the image will be rendered.  progressivepasses Progressive Passes integer When rendering in bucket mode (see imagemode), this is the number of progressive passes over the image to perform before switching to bucket mode. bucketsize Bucket Size integer Karma breaks down an image into multiple buckets for rendering. This is the side length (in pixels) of the square bucket. The default is 32, specifying a 32 pixel x 32 pixel bucket. Threads operate at the bucket level, so it might be useful to lower the bucket size if there are only a few buckets that are particularly expensive. That way the expensive areas can be divided across more threads. bucketorder Bucket Order string Specifies which buckets are rendered first. Values can be:  usecacheratio Cache Limit integer Whether to use a fixed size cache (karma:global:cachesize) or whether to use a proportion of physical memory (karma:global:cacheratio). cacheratio Cache Memory Ratio float The proportion of physical memory Karma will use for its unified cache. cachesize Cache Size (MB) integer  abortmissingtexture Cancel Render if Missing Texture is Discovered toggle Turning on this option will cause Karma to stop the render with an error if it encounters a missing texture map exportcomponents Export Components string A space-separated list of shading component names that will be computed for export. If you have defined new component labels in your materials, these can be added to the list so that they are exported for per-component export planes. If you are not using some components, remove them from the list to improve render efficiency. diffusecomponents Diffuse Components string A space-separated list of component types that will behave like diffuse bounces. This will affect which reflection scope is used based on the ray type and also which bounce limit to use. Uncategorized component types are assumed to be reflections. refractcomponents Refract Components string A space-separated list of component types that will behave like refract bounces. This will affect which reflection scope is used based on the ray type and also which bounce limit to use. Uncategorized component types are assumed to be reflections. volumecomponents Volume Components string A space-separated list of component types that will behave like volume bounces. This will affect which reflection scope is used based on the ray type and also which bounce limit to use. Uncategorized component types are assumed to be reflections. ssscomponents SSS Components string A space-separated list of component types that will behave like subsurface scatter bounces. This will affect which reflection scope is used based on the ray type and also which bounce limit to use. Uncategorized component types are assumed to be reflections. execute Render to Disk button Renders with the last render control settings. This blocks Houdini until the render completes. renderpreview Render to MPlay button Render directly into an MPlay preview window, instead of to an image file. (You can save the image to disk from inside MPlay.) executebackground Render to Disk in Background button Renders with the last render control settings in a background process. renderdialog Controls... button Click to open a dialog that lets you launch a â€œone-offâ€� render with different frame range and dependency settings. trange Valid Frame Range ordinal  f Start/End/Inc float When Valid frame range is â€œRender frame rangeâ€� or â€œRender frame range (strict)â€�, the start and end frames (inclusive) and interval. foffset Preroll/Postroll/Inc float When Valid frame range is â€œRender stageâ€™s frame rangeâ€�, the number of frames before and after the stageâ€™s official start and end frame to save, and the interval between time samples. allframesatonce Render All Frames With a Single Process toggle Render all frames in a background process. Default is off. This allows continued interaction with Houdini while the render process runs. override_camera Override Camera string Scene graph path to the Camera prim to render from. If this is blank, the node uses the camera specified on the render settings primitive. outputimage Override Output Image image If this is not blank, render to this file path instead of the output specified in the RenderSettings prim. When starting a new render process for each frame, this parameter can use standard Houdini variables such as $F4 to specify unique per-frame image files. When Render All Frames With a Single Process is enabled, this parameter must pass an un-expanded frame specifier (such as $F4 or <FF>) to husk. This may require the use of a backslash to prevent variable expansion when evaluating the parameter. primpattern Primitives string A space-separated list of prim paths for the objects you want to act as hold-outs.  spacer Spacer label  quicksetup3   ordinal  primpath Rendersettings Primitive Path string The prim path of a USD Render Settings prim to use to set up the background and matte settings. The default is /Render/rendersettings, which is the default for where the Karma render node looks for render settings. If this prim doesnâ€™t already exist in the incoming stage, this node will create it. plate Plate image The file path of the background image to use.  s Scale vector2  Horizontal and vertical scaling factors for the background image. These are normalized relative to the rendered image size, so for example a horizontal scale of 1 is the width of the rendered image. t Translate vector2 Horziontal and vertical offsets for the background image. These are normalized relative to the rendered images size, so for example a horizontal offset of 0.25 moves the background image to the right 1/4 of the width of the rendered image. useoffscreentex Use Offscreen Texture toggle If the background plate does not perfectly cover the camera view, the â€œrealâ€� background (empty space) will show through. Use this to replace empty space with a texture. If you leave this off, the node will fill empty space with the Offscreen color instead. offscreentex Offscreen Texture image When Use offscreen texture is on, the file path of the texture image to use to cover empty space. offscreentex_rotate Rotate vector When Use offscreen texture is on, this sets the rotation of the offscreen texture in 3D space. offscreen_col Offscreen Color color When Use offscreen texture is off, the color to use for any â€œempty spaceâ€� if the background plate does not fully cover the camera view. labelparm Shader Parameters label  metallic Metallic float Values closer to 1 give the shader a more metallic appearance. reflect Reflectivity float Controls the reflectivity of surfaces facing the viewer. This is also affected by the Index of Refraction. rough Roughness float Controls how dull a surface appears. A value of 0.0 results in a smooth surface with perfectly sharp reflections. A value of 1.0 produces a completely dull surface. ior IOR float Higher values reflect more light and bend refraction rays more. shadows Shadows ordinal Whether to record all holdout shadows in a single AOV, or generate a separate AOV for each light LPE tag. diffuse Diffuse toggle Generate an AOV for diffuse bounces on holdout objects.  emission Emission toggle Generate an AOV for light emissions on holdout objects.  reflection Glossy Reflection toggle Generate an AOV for glossy reflections on holdout objects. When disabled, the background shader will become diffuse only, reflectivity and metallic shader parameters will be set to 0. reflectionocclusion Reflection Occlusion ordinal When Glossy Reflection is enabled, whether to record all holdout reflection occlusion in a single AOV, or generate a separate AOV for each light LPE tag.

    used when a custom shader generates alpha information without using the
    known GL alpha and texture parameters. If disabled or absent, the material
    is only considered transparent if one of the alpha parameters is less than 
    one, or the diffuse or opacity texture has non-opaque alpha. If no materials
    are considered transparent, a transparency pass is not performed. saTexture Diffuse Texture image  saMotionVectorTexture Motion Vector Texture image  fTime Time float  fSpeed Speed float  fDoubleMotionVector Apply Double MotionVector integer  fRows Rows float  fCols Columns float  fDistortion Distortion float

searchable_text: inputGeoType Source Geo Type ordinal Set the type of geometry you are trying to cut. cuttingGeoType Cutting Geo Type ordinal Set the type of geometry you are trying to cut the input geometry with. useConnectivity Use Source Mesh Connectivity toggle When enabled, cuts are assigned to a connected set of primitives by assigning it a Connectivity ID. However in some cases you may want to treat all disconnected meshes as a single mesh, in which case the Connectitivy ID is set to -1. This option when disabled, can provide a performance boost when dealing with many disconnected Source and Cutting Primitives. (Alternatively, you may use \ bindToNearestSourcePrim Bind Cuts to Nearest Source Primitive (Faster) toggle When enabled, cutting primitives check from their center which connected source primitives are closest and assigns only to those primitives. Other disconnected primitives are ignored for that cutting primitive. Disabled by default, which allows one cutting primitive to affect multiple disconnected meshes at once without allowing them to fuse. In case many disconnected Source and Cutting primitives are provided, this option can provide a performance boost. crossCutSurface Cross Cut for Planar Surfaces toggle When enabled, this option interpolates the intersection as an edge hull instead, based on the cutting surface normal direction. Useful when 2 coincident non-planar surfaces / primitives are used as source and cutting inputs. The Cross Cut Depth affects the depth of the edge hull. extractIntersectionPoints Cut with Intersection Points from Cutting Geo toggle When enabled, you can provide Polyline Source Geometry to both inputs. This will detect intersections between the polylines and inject points on the Source Geometry with these points. High snap distance may over-detect and confuse intersections with geometry points nearby. crossCutDepth Cross-Cut Depth float When using \ sepparm6 Separator separator  sourceGroup Source Geo Group string Specify a group selection of the Source Primitives that can be Cut using the Cutting Geo Input cuttingGroup Cutting Geo Group string Specify a group selection of the Cutting Primitives that are allowed to make cuts. Takes a primitive group when cutting with surfaces or polylines. Takes points groups when cutting with points, except if \ sepparm Separator separator  surfaceOutput Surface Output ordinal Determines the type of Output. To either inject New Points on edges, or to cut a surface with a spline. Is enabled when cutting surfaces with Poly Surfaces or Poly Curves. surfaceCuttingMethod Slicing Method ordinal Determines how Surfaces are cut with Surfaces, Boolean based Slicing or point injection in general is more efficient, but it cannot use snapping features. Polysplit mode does feature snapping support and can auto complete cuts that don't slice an entire surface. PolySplit mode can be limited by its slow processing speed on large pieces of geometry, and may require high precision mode be enabled on dense geometry. If you need to cut a dense mesh with a surface, boolean mode is prefered. surfaceCuttingMethod_Dummy Slicing Method ordinal Normally determines how Surfaces are cut with Surfaces. This keeps the geometry clean and intact. Also propagates edge and point groups to non-selected geometry. cuspCutEdges Cusp Cut Edges toggle When enabled, cusps the cut edges on surfaces, spliting the geometry at the cut. When cutting with points or polylines it helps register cuts, when the distance falls within this value. Even if the cutting geometry is not exactly on the source geometry. When cutting with surfaces this helps avoid sliver cuts in corners by snapping the cuts to the geometry. When precise cuts must be made, smaller values produce higher levels of precision. LimitProxTol Disable Tolerance for Polyline Intersection Checks toggle This value disables the Intersection Tolerance for all polyline intersection checks. Normally, these intersection checks are limited by a tolerance value. However, in some cases, especially with very dense cutting geometries, it may fail to detect intersections. Turning this off changes the checking behavior, but REQUIRES that both input geometries overlap perfectly and are planar to a cardinal world axis. Intersection Tolerance is enabled by default. lengththreshold Edge Length Threshold float When in Boolean Shatter Mode, Allows tiny edges to be collapsed if under this length.
